utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Mr. Kotur, a former VJ soldier, expressing the position in neutral terms, says two things on which I want your comment. First at paragraph 34. He says that there was an occasion when Pavkovic gave a speech in Pristina, I suppose encouraging morale, but in the course of which he said that, "As soon as the first NATO bombs fall on Kosovo, we will have to 'clean our back from the Albanians,'" which can be interpreted as meaning get rid of the Albanians. Do you know of any address by Pavkovic where such a thing was said?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about such a speech made by Pavkovic. Maybe it happened at a police battalion when he was touring units. Maybe it's something he said before them, policemen, but I was never present when Pavkovic made that kind of speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And then paragraphs 40 to 42, in summary as follows, the same soldier says this: That after the conflict with NATO had begun, that's in April of 1999, he was instructed - and I'm not going to identify the commander in open session - to clean the area of Albanians and send them all towards Korenica, because they were waited for by the MUP with a list of names of terrorists. The witness explains that it was clear to him that this was a cover-up story and that the purpose of the operation was to cleanse the villages. And then I'll read the next paragraph and give you a chance to comment. He said that the following units participated in the operation: The 63rd Parachute Brigade, part of the 52nd Battalion military police, and the PJP, the Special Police Unit, and that the first village that was sealed and where cleansing started was Dobros, that the operation started at 6.00 in the morning, lasted for two days until the following daily at 1700 hours or 1800 hours, and the soldier explains they went through several villages. "Hard to say how many villages we went through because sometimes we would find 4 houses, sometimes 20, sometimes 40, and one doesn't have to count villages to learn the names of villages." The area was predominantly Catholic and they operated in a range of a 3 kilometres frontage, PJP on the right, another group to the middle and left, and I shan't name those in open session. Is that account by this soldier of this operation that you now do remember accurate? Is it?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of it is accurate, but as far as objectives are concerned and why it was done, that part is not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Which part of it is accurate, please?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part that's correct is that army units were involved as well as special units of the police; PJP. But as for the existence of lists and that they were pushed somewhere, I don't know anything about that. His own commander should have explained it to him. I believe there was only one company-level unit from the 52nd Police Battalion. It was with Pavkovic and Lazarevic, whom they were securing, and there was only a small part of that unit left there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Are you conceding that there was, as described, an operation to drive people down this valley from west to east, conducted by the police and the army jointly?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. There was no such concept or such assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In paragraph 42 of the same document, we hear: "During the operation, we only encountered civilians, sometimes arriving in villages already empty because the civilians probably see smoke and hear machine-guns and flee." He describes how the mortar platoon was two or three kilometres behind in case there was contact with the KLA, but explains that hundreds of Albanian civilians were expelled on the first day and that, after they were expelled, their houses were set on fire in accordance with the order given. Is it true that hundreds of houses were set on fire?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no such information or knowledge that hundreds of houses were set on fire, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, how about some houses set on fire?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some probably were.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Why? Why set people's houses on fire, Mr. Kotur?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say set on fire, I mean that they were burnt accidentally during combat operations. I didn't mean that they were intentionally set on fire. I was not involved in the operation. I don't know, but definitely it's not true that hundreds of houses burned. Since the MUP was involved, maybe MUP was doing something I don't know about. I don't know that the army ever burned houses. I don't know it. I think it definitely doesn't hold as far as the army is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Kotur, in relation to Meja, for which there is a mass of evidence, as you know, from bodies like Human Rights Watch collecting witness statements, witnesses we've called, the bodies at Batajnica, for Meja there are two soldiers who have provided -- at least two, but two soldiers who have provided accounts explaining that this was ethnic cleansing with mass killing. And that's the truth, isn't it? That's what Meja was all about, was a revenge attack, ethnic cleansing, and mass killing.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not accept that for the simple reason that that operation did not have such an objective. And if at the end of the operation something happened, that had not been planned, one; and two, we were not informed of any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll ask a few questions about the notebook we've been able to identify. I simply don't have time. I see the Court may be concerned about that, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, Mr. Nice, the second statement of Nik Peraj --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- was that exhibited?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the same number, 143?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: According to our records, yes. In fact there were three statements. The last statement's a correction statement, which dealt with a few typographical errors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, I'm reminded that you're now using almost 100 per cent of the time spent by the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm quite aware of that. The Chamber will have -- so sorry. The Chamber will have in mind the way the answers have been given and the topics that have been covered. And as to this particular document, it's a document we wanted a long time ago. It's apparently the only record we're going to get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're getting to a stage where it's actually going to be impossible for you to comply with the order that was made about time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It's going to be difficult. We have it in mind as a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's -- I find it very difficult to see how you are if you continue to continue cross-examination at this length.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the Court's -- I'm in the Court's hands, to a degree, and I ask the Court to be understanding of the difficulties we face when we're not provided in advance with material and statements that enable us to know what's coming. This is a document that may be of interest to the Chamber, I don't know. We've been able to look at it and there are a couple of entries in it -- there are quite a number of entries, they probably boil down to a few topics. What should we do? Leave it altogether? Ask for it to be translated and made available post facto when the witness can't deal with it, or simply abandon the prospect asking any questions on it altogether? It seems to me, where there is such a dearth of contemporaneous material evidence associated with this witness, that the Chamber might be helped by hearing one or two things, but I'm not going to press it. If the Chamber is against me, I'm quite happy to stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, no doubt that's right. The issue is a much broader strategic issue. It's not an issue related to this one subject about which you're about to cross-examine. You have to give thought to how you approach cross-examination in general if you're going to assist the Chamber to ensure that its order is implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Well, it's always been our desire to maintain the ratio of time that the Court wanted, and indeed to better it, but there are real practical problems where we are presented with the sort of evidence we are presented, and it would have been wholly wrong not, for example, to have taken this witness to the evidence about Meja which implicates him even though he didn't deal with it in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How much longer will you be now?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm actually prepared to abandon the book. Just let me just take one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I ask a few general -- just a couple of general questions that I know arise from the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let a copy be provided to the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There is no copy, there's just one document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Just this: Your book shows, doesn't it, Mr. Kotur, throughout the relevant period gathering up reservists 600 at a time. That's not rotation, that's preparing for war ahead of the end of March and in contravention of the agreement; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we interpreted the agreement that had been signed, it was not contrary to it. It's true the reservists were coming in to be trained. Yesterday, I started saying but I didn't finish there was an assessment made in March by the corps command concerning the strength of the so-called KLA under arms, and the number of villages affected by combat operations, about our operative and tactical position of the corps itself - it was assessed as very unfavourable - and on the basis of that assessment and taking into account -- let me tell you which document it is. It was signed --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Can I cut the witness short. I have two questions I want to ask him. I'd ask the document be made available for translation, we have it translated and consider its potential as an exhibit later on if that's acceptable. It's the only way we can get through things quickly. But there are two entries. Can we just look at this entry. Mr. Nort, that entry and that entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Read them out and interpret them for us because they will need your interpretation. That one and that one. First one, please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Search of the terrain south of Junik. Participation in the blockade of a terrorist group. No changes in mobility."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No, finish. That's enough.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Plan of drills not received. You ask for it. Course for squad commanders, method-wise it --"

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "-- does not hold."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Could you read the word "pretres of the terrain" out. And if so, what -- just read "pretres" again. I'm not sure you read that.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Search of the terrain."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... interpretation. Next entry, please. Just read the second entry I pointed to.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Damjane village photographed. Combat Group 3."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter doesn't know how to interpret this. Something involving force.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Nikodin village near Urosevac, explosion. Admission of reservists and their briefing. Plan of disinformation and deceit."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... without more time than I'm prepared to devote in light of the concern of the Court and without parallel documents to go to work from in photocopy form, I'd ask that the document be made available, we'll have it translated, and then we will address the issue of its being an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you Mr. Nice. Mr. Milosevic, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Colonel Kotur, would you please take this document placed before you by Mr. Nice entitled "Daily operative report of the 15th of January, 1991 [as interpreted], General Staff of the army of Yugoslavia, department for operations." Do you have that document?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have it. I returned it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May it be given to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: 1999, not 1991, as is on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought I said 1999. Maybe it was a slip of the tongue. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the record, it is Exhibit 934.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Have you received it now?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Look at page 2, item 8.4, because that's the only thing that refers to the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I received the wrong document, dated the 10th of March. I see it only now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found it. What point did you want me to take a look at?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Point 8.4. Just the section referring to the 3rd Army. So it's the paragraph, a very short one beginning with 3rd Army. The first thing it says is -- or you can read it out.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "During tactical exercises on a mechanised company of the Urosevac 243rd Mechanised Brigade in the sector of Dulje, near the village of Sefer, the Siptar terrorists opened fire with infantry weapons after which they retreated towards the Dara Glava feature. Our forces were unharmed."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that, then, is a tactical exercise that was going on; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And it was being performed by part of the unit at Dulje; is that right? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, just for my benefit, just say what a tactical exercise is. No, no, not you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's a regular --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A tactical exercise means training the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's what they're doing with the object of training the troops.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says that there were no consequences, and all this took place near the village of Sefer. That's what it says. Now, was this an event which was completely separate from the one in Racak?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Or does it have anything to do with Racak?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is at the Dulje pass, which means separate from Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. But we're talking about that same combat group that was at Dulje near Stimlje and Canovic hill; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was divided in two parts; one was at Stimlje, one was at Canovic hill or, rather, Dulje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, this other part, this second part, does it refer to the combat group that was at Canovic group, because it says some of the forces the BG-243-1 were deployed to seal off or block the village of Racak.

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's part of the group, of that same group.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us, please, since when was that part of the group located in the area stipulated?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at that location since 1998. That is to say, the month of April 1998, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, the deployment and disposition of that part of the Tactical Group, did it have anything at all to do with the operation or, rather, the anti-terrorist action in Racak?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was there for several months. It went on for several months and wasn't exclusively intended for Racak. It wasn't intended to be there for Racak but to control and provide safety along the communication lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, if there is an anti-terrorist operation in the close vicinity, it's very existence in that locality, could that be considered blocking off an access or sealing off an access?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that. Its very existence can be interpreted as having blocked the region, blocked the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Now it goes on to say the village of Racak, the Stimlje municipality, that's just an identification, Racak is the essential point, and then what does it say?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Where the MUP members conducted an operation against Siptar terrorists who had killed a MUP member."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Fine. Now, does it say quite literally here that the operation was carried out by members of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in an operative report of this department for operations, had the army taken part would it have necessarily said members of the MUP and units of the army of Yugoslavia, such-and-such a unit had a unit been there and taken part in that action?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would have been the normal way to formulate it in a report. If they had taken part together, then it would have said the MUP and the army, that they had taken part together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you're saying that that would have had to have been recorded?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what does it say here?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that it was only the MUP members who launched this operation against the Siptar terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, these questions are either tendentious or leading in effect and form. We can see exactly where the accused is going. He knows how he can ask questions neutrally if he wants to. The last one is quite a good example of how he can get away with it, really. He asks where something might have happened, and then the next question is - what is it he said? - "It would have had to have been recorded in that way." It's all pretty clear, but there it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, reformulate the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: If it says here "who launched and conducted the operation" can we then imply that somebody had taken part in it who wasn't recorded here, who hasn't been written down here?

utterances.speaker: MILAN KOTUR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already given an explanation about that in my previous response, that the people conducting the operation are included here and written down here. Anybody who wasn't included was not written down here. Now, part of the blockade or support - and I explained earlier on that those are two different things; support means one thing, blockade means another, or to seal off means another - when I discussed paragraph 8 or, rather, point 8.
